verses.1: Oh you who are a lover, but you yourself are not a lover. You speak falsely and do not tell the truth. Your love is nothing but hypocrisy; your lovers will surely betray you.
verses.2: May Jehovah protect us. May they be a seed for the future; may they save us in times of distress.
verses.3: From the sound of the horn, nations were scattered from your land; nations were destroyed.
verses.4: And they gathered together for your sake. They gathered like bees that buzz around in their hives.
verses.5: YHWH is disgraced, because He has brought about chaos and injustice from His own laws and justice.
verses.6: And there will be truthfulness among you at that time. There will also be salvation, wisdom, knowledge, and fear of the Lord. These will be your blessings.
verses.7: And they also cried out in pain, as if they were victims of great suffering. Mer Yivkayun.
verses.8: Let them be freed from the bonds of slavery. Let them leave behind the obligations of a covenant that has been broken. They do not think about us at all.
verses.9: But the land was desolate and barren. The trees were like weeds, and the vines were withered.
verses.10: Now I will stand up and say, “YHWH, now let them be destroyed. Now, let them be taken away.”
verses.11: Be careful! May you be born with great difficulties. Fire will consume you.
verses.12: And there were nations whose people were burned to death; they were destroyed by fire.
verses.13: Hear from afar what I have done, and know that my judgments are near.
verses.14: They feared the sins of Zion; they trembled with fear. Who will shut us in? Who will put fire between us? Who will destroy us forever?
verses.15: He walks in righteousness, and his words are from those who are pure. He acts with compassion towards others. His hands are filled with compassion; his ears cannot hear the cries of the poor. His eyes see only evil.
verses.16: He makes stones stand on their sides, and he gives them strength from his hands.
verses.17: In his beauty, we shall see the king. Your eyes shall behold a land far away.
verses.18: Your heart will be filled with fear. Who is the writer of this book? Who measures its length and width?
verses.19: Do not see those who mock others as people with a thick speech. They are like pigs that are laughed at; there’s nothing noble about them at all.
verses.20: Look, Zion will be rescued from our hands. Your eyes will see Jerusalem rise again. The temple of Balak will be rebuilt. His enemies will be destroyed forever, and all his followers will be saved.
verses.21: For there, in that place, will be the great God who gives us a place where rivers flow, wide plains where we can rest. But I, a poor man, cannot cross over there. It’s too difficult for me.
verses.22: For the LORD will judge us; the LORD will condemn us. The LORD will rule over us; He will save us.
verses.23: Your soldiers were defeated; they were not able to strengthen themselves. They were also scattered everywhere. Then, many days of fasting passed by.
verses.24: And when they said, “I’m sick,” the people who lived there became terrified.
